verdict.rationale: Teller documents its own REST API for retrieving live balances and ledger transactions, with mTLS client-certificate authentication, so an agent could programmatically read account data. Link sessions run through the Teller Connect front-end component rather than a documented API call. There is no evidence of connection-management endpoints, an MCP surface, or credentials scoped for agents, and probes found no llms.txt or OpenAPI spec. Missing for 10: API-driven link-session creation, documented enrollment/connection management endpoints, an MCP server, scoped/least-privilege agent credentials, a machine-readable API spec.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, an agent can operate the platform — create link sessions, retrieve balances and transactions, and manage connections through the API or an MCP surface with scoped credentials

citations.quote: The account balances API provides your application with live, real-time account balances.
The transactions API exposes the ledger transactions of a financial account.
The Teller API uses mTLS to authenticate the API caller. Teller issues client certificates that you use to connect to the Teller API.
